rationale: S7 method registration is a function call on the LEFT of an assignment: `S7::method(format, Temperature) <- function(object, ...)`. The bound "name" is a CALL, so the identifier rule that finds every other R declaration cannot see it at all -- S7 is the object system ggplot2 and dplyr write today and 31 method definitions appear in ggplot2 alone. The second and third registrations are the hard part: S7 dispatches on a SET of classes and the owner must come from the FIRST named class in `list(Reading, Writing)`. `Writing` is forbidden as an owner so an implementation that takes the last element, or joins the list into one name, is caught; `Reading` is pinned as the owner twice, once per registration, because the two `format` methods are different functions with the same name and only the owner distinguishes them. `object@celsius` is an S4-style slot read of an S7 object and is a `uses` edge to the bare member name, so it binds to the same `celsius` property symbol that `new_class(properties=)` published -- that join is the whole reason the `uses` type exists.
